AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this study was to search for possible criteria for obesity in Japanese college student athletes by examining insulin resistance.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The subjects were 219 male college students (mean age 20.4 ± 1.3 years), including 119 athletes who belonged to a university sports team and 100 non-athletic individuals who did not. Fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), fasting insulin and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) levels were examined in relationship to body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference (WC).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Although none of the subjects had diabetes mellitus, 15 (5 athletes (4.2%) and 10 non-athletes (10.0%)) had insulin resistance with HOMA-IR ≥2.5. HOMA-IR was significantly higher in athletes with BMI ≥27.0 kg/m(2) and non-athletes with BMI ≥25.0 kg/m(2) than in subjects with BMI <25.0 kg/m(2). A similar pattern was seen for WC ≥90 cm in athletes and ≥85 cm in non-athletes. Nearly all athletes with increased insulin resistance had BMI ≥27.0 kg/m(2) and WC ≥90 cm. Among non-athletes, nine of the 10 subjects with insulin resistance had BMI ≥25.0 kg/m(2) and WC ≥85 cm. According to these criteria, the sensitivity and specificity were nearly 100% and 93% for athletes, and 90% and 70% for non-athletes, respectively.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Japanese college athletes may be at risk for increased insulin resistance when BMI exceeds 27.0 kg/m(2) and WC exceeds 90 cm.
